title: Urinary tract infection: cystitis, pyelonephritis, and when not to treat

source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-09-13. Based on IDSA guidance on cystitis, pyelonephritis and asymptomatic bacteriuria. Not tied to an article; review before trusting.

questions.q: Which are first-line regimens for uncomplicated cystitis in a woman?
questions.why: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is first-line only where local resistance is under 20%. Fluoroquinolones are reserved because of resistance and tendon, nerve and aortic harms.

questions.q: Why is nitrofurantoin not used for pyelonephritis?
questions.a: It does not reach adequate levels in kidney tissue
d: It only works against gram-positive organisms
questions.why: It concentrates in urine, which is exactly right for cystitis and wrong for an infected kidney. It is also avoided with a creatinine clearance under 30.

questions.q: For outpatient pyelonephritis treated with ciprofloxacin, how long is the course?
questions.why: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole needs 14 days. Where fluoroquinolone resistance exceeds 10%, a single dose of intravenous ceftriaxone is given first.

questions.q: In which situations should a urine culture be sent before treating?
d: A first uncomplicated cystitis in a healthy woman
questions.why: Uncomplicated cystitis is treated on symptoms alone. Anything complicated, recurrent, or at risk of resistance needs a culture to guide therapy.

questions.q: Asymptomatic bacteriuria should be treated in which patients?
a: Patients about to have a urological procedure with mucosal bleeding
d: Kidney transplant recipients after the first months
questions.why: In everyone else treatment breeds resistance and Clostridioides difficile without preventing anything. Pyuria alone is not an indication either.

questions.q: A patient with a catheter in place for three weeks has fever and a positive urine culture. What should happen before treating?
questions.a: Replace the catheter and send the culture from the new one
d: Treat based on the existing culture
Remove the catheter and do not replace it
questions.why: Biofilm on an old catheter grows organisms that are not causing the infection. Fever without another source is the trigger to treat; pyuria and smell are not.

questions.q: For how long is cystitis in a man usually treated?
questions.why: Infection in a man is treated as complicated, with a culture. A prostatic source is considered when there is fever, perineal pain or recurrence, and then the course is longer.

questions.q: Which antibiotics are avoided for cystitis in pregnancy?
questions.why: Nitrofurantoin is avoided near term because of neonatal haemolysis. Bacteriuria is screened for at 12 to 16 weeks because untreated it leads to pyelonephritis and preterm birth.

questions.q: A postmenopausal woman has three culture-proven cystitis episodes in a year. Which preventive measure has the best evidence?
questions.why: Continuous or post-coital low-dose antibiotic prophylaxis is the next option. Cranberry has weak and mixed evidence; increased fluid intake helps a little.

questions.q: On a urine dipstick, which finding is the more specific for infection?
questions.why: Nitrite needs a nitrate-reducing organism such as E. coli and several hours in the bladder, so it is often negative in true infection. Leukocyte esterase is sensitive but not specific.

questions.q: A woman treated for cystitis is well after her course. Should a test-of-cure urine be sent?
questions.a: No; resolution of symptoms is the end point
d: Yes, a culture at one week
Yes, a dipstick at one week
questions.why: Test of cure is only for pregnancy. A positive follow-up culture in an asymptomatic woman would just be bacteriuria, which is not treated.

questions.q: Pyelonephritis is not improving after 48 to 72 hours of appropriate antibiotics. What is the next step?
d: Extend the same antibiotic to 21 days
questions.why: An obstructed infected kidney is an emergency that needs drainage. A CT or ultrasound is also indicated at presentation for anyone with a stone history, diabetes or sepsis.
